title: Microsoft Teams: separate attendance and engagement report policy for Teams events
summary: Hold: the open questions incorrectly say Microsoft has not published event-report licensing or a GCC rollout window. Microsoft documents report capabilities by licence, and its tenant notice gives Worldwide and GCC the same rollout schedule; the core policy description and controls are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans separate event-report controls in CsTeamsEventsPolicy, independent of meeting-report controls in CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.
claims.quote: administrators can independently manage organizer access to attendance and engagement reports for Teams Events through CsTeamsEventsPolicy, without affecting attendance and engagement report settings for Teams Meetings managed through CsTeamsMeetingPolicy.

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy supports -Identity and -AllowEngagementReport with Enabled, Disabled, ForceEnabled and ForceDisabled to control event reporting.
claims.quote: -Identity: Unique identifier assigned to the Teams Events policy. -AllowEngagementReport: Controls whether attendance and engagement reports are allowed for events. Possible values are: Enabled; Disabled; ForceEnabled; ForceDisabled.

claims.claim: The events parameter value Enabled means On, but organizers can turn it off.
claims.quote: Enabled: On, but organizers can turn it off.

claims.claim: The events parameter value Disabled means Off, but organizers can turn it on.
claims.quote: Disabled: Off, but organizers can turn it on.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No Teams admin center path is documented for the new events-policy attendance setting at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "events" "attendance" "Events policies" "Attendance and engagement report"; "Teams" "events policy" "attendance" "admin center". Opened attendance-report, meeting-policies-overview, plan-events and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; only the meeting-policy reporting path was found.

claims.claim: The current meeting-report setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Meeting scheduling > Attendance and engagement report.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. 2. Select the policy you want to update or create a new policy. 3. Go to the Meeting scheduling section. 4. Choose one of the following options for Attendance and engagement report
claims.fix: Insert the policy-selection step in the front matter and rendered table: Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting scheduling > Attendance and engagement report.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy supports -Identity and -AllowEngagementReport with Disabled, Enabled and ForceEnabled for current meeting reporting.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport Disabled
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport ForceEnabled
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowEngagementReport Enabled

claims.claim: Administrators cannot view attendance and engagement reports for events they did not organise.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can’t view the attendance and engagement report for meetings and events that you didn't organize. However, you can view attendees' details for a given meeting or event within 24 hours of that meeting or event.
claims.fix: Retain the report-access restriction, but qualify the conclusion: administrators can still view participant details within 24 hours through Users > Manage users > organizer > Meetings & calls > meeting or call > Participant details. This is not access to the report itself.

claims.claim: The setting governs human report access rather than introducing an autonomous action.
claims.quote: Controls whether attendance and engagement reports are allowed for events.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence or meter specific to the new events-policy setting itself, so its licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "CsTeamsEventsPolicy" "AllowEngagementReport" "license". Opened Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy, attendance-report and events-licensing; read roadmap and MC1455014. Report licensing exists, but no setting-specific licence or meter was found.

claims.claim: The attendance-report page says a tenant needs at least one active Teams Premium licence to manage Teams Premium features.
claims.quote: To manage Teams Premium features, your tenant must have at least one active Teams Premium license.

claims.claim: The attendance-report page's generic Teams Premium note does not identify attendance reporting itself as a Premium-only feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "CsTeamsEventsPolicy" "AllowEngagementReport" "license"; opened the complete attendance-report article and events-licensing. The attendance article's Premium note does not classify the reports; events-licensing separately classifies attendance and engagement reporting.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether an existing meeting-policy restriction will be copied into the events policy at rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: "AllowEngagementReport" "events" "inherit"; Teams events CsTeamsEventsPolicy attendance report AllowTrackingInReport migration inherit meeting policy. Read MC1455014, attendance-report and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy; no migration or copy rule was found.

claims.claim: The researched Learn documentation does not name a required administrator role for editing the new events reporting setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "CsTeamsEventsPolicy" "AllowEngagementReport" "role"; "Teams events policy" "administrator role". Opened Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy, meeting-policies-overview and plan-events; no named required role for this setting was found.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy documents -InfoShownInReportMode alongside -AllowEngagementReport.
claims.quote:
[-AllowEngagementReport <String>]
[-InfoShownInReportMode <String>]
-InfoShownInReportMode: Controls what information is shown in attendance reports.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy syntax lists no attendee-inclusion parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events CsTeamsEventsPolicy attendance report AllowTrackingInReport migration inherit meeting policy. Read the Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy syntax and searched its full reference for AllowTrackingInReport; only AllowEngagementReport and InfoShownInReportMode were listed for reporting.

claims.claim: Whether GCC receives the setting at the same time as Worldwide is unstated beyond the roadmap cloud list.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout will begin in mid-December 2026 (previously early November) and is expected to complete by early January 2027 (previously early December 2026)
claims.fix: Remove this open question and its assertion of missing information. State that MC1455014 gives Worldwide and GCC the same planned rollout window, mid-December 2026 through early January 2027; this does not promise simultaneous activation in every tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether a licence is required for event reports.
claims.quote: All eligible Teams licenses include the foundational capabilities needed to create and run events, engage attendees, review attendance reports, and publish event recordings.
claims.fix: Replace this open question with the published distinction at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing: Attendance reports are foundational; Attendance and engagement reports are advanced event features. Cite that page and its eligible-licence table. Keep any unknown limited to separate licensing for the new policy setting itself, not the reports it governs.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits the standard for the verified rollout and medium risk.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; risk: "medium"; "If nobody acts, event organisers get the new setting's default"; "rollout begins in mid-December 2026".
claims.fix: Set action to act-now under the schema's approximately-60-day rule: on 16 November 2026 the automatic mid-December rollout is about one month away, risk is medium, and administrators have a reporting-policy decision to make. This is a wiki action rating, not a Microsoft act-by deadline.
